rootCause.summary: WorkerSupervisor.stop() issued a single lifecycleRequest('stop-authority') with an empty catch block. The single lifecycle pipe is shared by the 1-second health/discovery probe started by carrierReady(). When the health discover occupied the lifecycle pipe at stop time, openLifecycle -> inspectLocalPlatform observed lifecycleBusy=true and threw BUSY. The empty catch swallowed it, the stop-authority request never reached the Helper/Worker, and the 8-second PID poll returned exited=false with Worker/Host/Helper still alive.
timeline: carrierReady() starts setInterval health discover every 1000ms; each discover holds the single lifecycle pipe from createConnection until socket.destroy (including two native child-process inspections).
Electron teardown: maybeFinalizeEvidence() calls carrier.close() then supervisor.stop().
stop() calls detach() (clears the interval) but an already-in-flight discover continues to hold the pipe.
stop() calls lifecycleRequest('stop-authority') -> openLifecycle -> inspectLocalPlatform (native --platform) -> WaitNamedPipeW returns busy -> lifecycleBusy=true -> throw BUSY.
BUSY is swallowed by the empty catch {}; the stop-authority frame is never written.
stop() polls process exit for 8 seconds; Worker/Host/Helper remain alive -> exited=false.

codeLocations.busySource: apps/desktop/src/main/lifecycle-client.ts openLifecycle(): if (platform.lifecycleBusy) throw new Error('BUSY')
codeLocations.busyDetection: apps/native-carrier/WindowsAuthority.cs Platform(): lifecycleBusy = pipeError is 121 or 231

deterministicReproduction.method: Start real Worker authority, attach Carrier, hold a lifecycle connection via openLifecycle (the identical mechanism the health discover uses), then call stop().

rootCause.correlatedPreviousEvidence: STEP1-20260909-IMPLEMENTATION-01/electron-regression.json recorded cleanup.exited=false with a healthy DETACHED authority still alive; a later isolated direct stop succeeded, confirming a transient occupancy rather than a broken stop protocol.

notAssumed: The BUSY root cause was established by deterministic reproduction capturing the actual swallowed exception (BUSY), not by source inspection alone. The hypothesis that an in-flight health discover occupies the pipe is consistent with the code (the health discover is the only concurrent lifecycle client) and with the observed real teardown failure.
